headline: Trump rejects Iran ceasefire; BTC holds $84.0k, oil's -7.4% week now mispriced
summary: At 14:56 UTC on Saturday 26 September the tape is flat but the news underneath it turned: BTC is $84,026.60 against an $84,090.50 open (-0.08%), ETH $2,689.00 (-0.09%) and SOL $120.97 (-0.94%), all sitting in the upper half of narrow session ranges (BTC 70% up $83,351.50-$84,314.70, ETH 68% up $2,668.33-$2,698.71, SOL 50% up $119.01-$122.91), with weekly changes of +3.2% BTC, +1.8% ETH and +8.2% SOL. The change since the last briefing is geopolitical: Trump said today he rejected Iran's seven-day roadmap - reopen the Strait of Hormuz on day six, restart nuclear talks on day seven, in exchange for lifting the naval blockade and easing oil sanctions - calling it unacceptable and saying Tehran wants it "because they have no money coming in"; the Wall Street Journal reports he told people close to him he expects to restart bombing after the November midterms and will not lift the blockade. That matters mechanically because WTI fell 7.4% last week to $92.41 on the premise of exactly that deal, so the whole de-escalation discount is now sitting in oil with nothing behind it, and oil futures reopen Sunday evening into a weekend that also saw Saudi-led forces intercept two Houthi drones headed for Riyadh and two ballistic missiles aimed at Khamis Mushait. Crypto's own reaction has been contained rather than panicked - BTC slid 3.8% from Tuesday's $87,395 high to a $83,000-$84,000 test, total liquidations were $255m today with only $63m in BTC, and the underlying bid is the strongest in a year: US spot bitcoin ETFs took $2.39bn over 21-25 September, the biggest week since October 2025 (IBIT $1.16bn, FBTC $701m), while Binance saw 13,800 BTC leave in a single day, the largest outflow since 2023. Fear & Greed is 74 and the composite 65.2, both Greed, but the book is not crowded: Hyperliquid funding is a uniform 0.00125%/h on all three, futures trade at a discount to spot on BTC (-0.036%) and SOL (-0.015%) and flat on ETH, and only 54 items came through in 24 hours - so the risk here is a Sunday-night gap, not an existing dip.

BTC.note: $84,026.60, down 0.08% on the session and 70% up an $83,351.50-$84,314.70 range on $3.16bn of open interest, funding 0.00125%/h and a -0.036% futures discount to spot - no live dip trigger, and the 3.8% slide from Tuesday's $87,395 high has been absorbed sideways rather than sold.

ETH.note: $2,689.00, off 0.09% inside a $30 session range and still the laggard at +1.8% on the week against BTC's +3.2%, on $2.95bn of open interest and a futures premium of exactly zero - no seller urgency, no buyer urgency either.

SOL.note: $120.97, down 0.94% from a $122.12 open and the only one of the three really moving; the flush to $119.01 was bought back to mid-range, it is +8.2% on the week and the strongest of the three, and open interest of $688.6m with a -0.015% discount says give-back after a rally, not distribution.

drivers.title: Trump rejects Iran's seven-day Hormuz roadmap; WSJ says bombing resumes after midterms
drivers.detail: Trump said on Saturday 26 September that he has rejected Iran's proposal - submitted via Qatari mediators by foreign minister Abbas Araghchi, reopening the Strait of Hormuz on day six and resuming nuclear talks on day seven in exchange for lifting the US naval blockade, unfreezing assets and easing oil sanctions - calling it unacceptable: "They want to make a deal where they open the strait immediately because they're losing so badly... they have no money coming in." He described the blockade as "the greatest blockade ever in military history, a wall of steel", said 29 ships came out of the strait overnight, and posted "IRAN CAN NOT HAVE A NUCLEAR WEAPON!!!" on Truth Social at 13:38 UTC. The Wall Street Journal reports he told people close to him he expects to restart bombing after the November midterms and will not lift the blockade; separately the Saudi-led coalition intercepted two Houthi drones aimed at Riyadh and two ballistic missiles aimed at Khamis Mushait early today.

drivers.title: Oil's 7.4% weekly fall priced the deal that was just refused
drivers.detail: WTI closed Friday 25 September at $92.41, down $2.20 (-2.33%) on the day and about 7.4% on the week, a decline built almost entirely on reports of US-Iran technical contacts and a phased Hormuz reopening, with Hormuz flows at 33.7m barrels for the week. With the roadmap now rejected and the blockade staying in place, that de-escalation discount has no support, and oil and index futures reopen Sunday evening - the single most likely source of a gap that drags the 10-year and crypto with it. This is the mirror image of last week's setup, where falling oil was the argument for lower yields.

drivers.title: Best ETF week since October 2025: $2.39bn in, and 13,800 BTC off Binance
drivers.detail: US spot bitcoin ETFs took $2.39bn over the 21-25 September week, the largest weekly inflow since October 2025, with IBIT at $1.16bn and FBTC at $701m, its best since September 2025; Friday alone was +$134.46m for a seventh straight inflow day (IBIT +$96.99m, FBTC +$49.32m, BITB -$11.85m) on $108.42bn of total net assets. In the same window Binance saw 13,800 BTC leave in a single day, its largest outflow since 2023, with reserves falling from about 705,000 to 685,000 BTC. Direction is the point: coins are moving off exchanges and into wrappers while the news flow deteriorates, which is what separates this from a structural break.

drivers.title: 10-year near 5.17% and 64-70% odds of an October hike still cap the range
drivers.detail: The US 10-year Treasury yield sits near 5.17%, a 19-year high, after finishing Friday around 5.163% and touching 5.205% on Thursday, the most since June 2007. CME FedWatch prices a further 25bp hike at the 27-28 October FOMC at about 64%, with other venues 67-70%, supported by Wednesday's 58.4 S&P Global composite PMI, the strongest in more than five years. CoinDesk noted on 25 September that bond volatility surged while bitcoin and equities stayed calm; an oil-led yield push next week is the mechanism that would close that divergence against crypto.

drivers.title: Bitget reopens BTC withdrawals Monday 08:00 UTC, with a 10% recovery bounty
drivers.detail: Bitget's staged restart after the 24 September breach begins Monday 28 September at 08:00 UTC with Bitcoin, then ETH on the 29th, USDT on the 30th and other tokens, fiat and P2P on 2 October. Unauthorised transfers were revised from about $351.6m to roughly $387.5m; the exchange says the vulnerability is patched, Mandiant and SlowMist are investigating, the Protection Fund holding more than $464m covers the loss, and it has added a bounty of up to 10% on frozen or recovered funds. CEO Gracy Chen says the patterns resemble groups previously linked to North Korea, without confirmed attribution. Circle and Tether have frozen only 218,023 USDT and 99,990 USDC.

drivers.title: The book is de-levered: $255m liquidated today, funding flat, futures at a discount
drivers.detail: Total crypto liquidations were $255m on 26 September with bitcoin only $63m of that, against $560m on 24 September when BTC first broke below $84,000 - the selling is getting smaller, not larger. Hyperliquid funding is a uniform 0.00125%/h on BTC, ETH and SOL, BTC and SOL futures trade at a discount to spot (-0.036% and -0.015%) and ETH at exactly flat, open interest is $3.16bn / $2.95bn / $689m, and only 54 items came through in 24 hours. For a dip buyer this is the favourable half of the picture: the history file records 92.9% of 28 BTC dips recovering +1.5% within 14 days (median 5.0 h, 78.6% inside 24 h, typical extra drop -0.5%), and 100% of the 7 that happened during greed, which is the regime Fear & Greed 74 puts us in now.

watch.what: Oil and index futures reopen for the week. This is the first price that sees Trump's rejection of the Hormuz roadmap, after WTI had already fallen 7.4% last week on the assumption a deal was coming. A gap up in crude pushes the 10-year off 5.17% and is the most plausible route to a genuine crypto dip in the next 48 hours.

Bitget reopens Bitcoin withdrawals, the first of four stages. The loss estimate already moved once, from $351.6m to $387.5m, so a queue that clears quietly removes the last acute crypto-specific risk while a second delay is the clearest candidate for a panic flush this week.

The rest of the Bitget restart at 08:00 UTC each day: ETH on the 29th, USDT on the 30th, other tokens, fiat and P2P on 2 October. The USDT stage on the 30th is the one that would show up in stablecoin pricing if anything goes wrong.

Quarter-end data cluster: US personal income and outlays with the PCE deflator, ADP private payrolls, the final Q2 GDP estimate and JOLTS openings, plus Chinese PMIs and flash euro-zone CPI. With October hike odds at 64-70% and the 10-year at a 19-year high, a firm PCE is the most direct scheduled pressure on the yield capping this range.
ISM Manufacturing PMI and weekly jobless claims, the warm-up to Friday's payrolls after Wednesday's 58.4 composite PMI already lifted hike odds.

September employment report (08:30 ET), consensus near +100k nonfarm payrolls from +162k with unemployment ticking to 4.2%. A hot print into a Fed already 64-70% priced to hike is the clearest macro route to a dip; the same day is Hester Peirce's last at the SEC, cutting the commission to Atkins and Uyeda after the CLARITY Act cloture vote failed.

Any Iranian response to the rejection - Houthi launches at Riyadh and Khamis Mushait were intercepted this morning, and the WSJ report that US strikes resume after the November midterms means the next escalation step is now assumed rather than negotiated away. Watch for tanker incidents and new Treasury sanctions on Iranian crypto networks, which have moved BTC before.

FOMC rate decision (2:00 p.m. ET, meeting 27-28 October), about 64-70% priced for a further 25bp hike. The US-China truce now runs to 10 January 2027, so tariffs are not competing for attention before then.
